newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up in slow trading on Wednesday on short-covering triggered by improved sentiment on the London Metal Exchange overnight, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,370 yuan ($2,452) per tonne, rising 70 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 20,250 and hit a high of 20,420.
September rose 50 to 21,230, October 130 to 20,780, November 120 to 20,550, December 80 to 20,400, the February 1997 contract 90 to 20,390 and April 90 to 20,420.
Combined volume fell to 15,060 tonnes from 40,730.
Copper opened mostly up and short-covering pushed the prices up further during the rest of the session.
"Some speculators were eager to liquidate their short positions because copper did not breach the key $1,900-support level last night on the LME," one trader said.
"They were disappointed because they had expected sharp falls over the past few days," he added.
Traders said the thin volume indicated most investors were uncertain about the short-term trend and copper would continue moving between 20,000 and 20,500 in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. September fell 180 to 13,980 yuan, October 110 to 14,150 and November 150 to 14,120.
Combined volume rose to 1,900 tonnes from 460.
